svg.text: How fast must a flying fish go to stay up, and how fast does it go?
Minimum lift-supported speed from one measured specimen; each bar is a published speed, source on hover. No bird data.

rect.title: Pre-registered band [v_min, 3 v_min] = [9.85, 29.56] m/s. v_min = sqrt(2W/(rho S C_Lmax)) with W 0.5886 N, S 0.01269 m2, C_Lmax 0.78 (Park and Choi 2010, Table 1 model L3 and Table 2, retrieved 2026-10-31T18:18:51Z), rho 1.225 kg/m3. Computed by physics/analysis.py.

line.title: Descriptive only: v_min 14.4 m/s for a 0.226 kg Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini over 0.0225 m2 (Kawachi et al. 1993 as quoted by Deng et al. 2019) with the C_Lmax borrowed from Park and Choi 2010.

svg.text: wind-tunnel free stream: Cypselurus hiraii model

circle.title: 12 m/s. measured. Source: park-choi-2010 (Materials and methods: free-stream velocity 12 m/s), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:18:51Z. Method: wind tunnel. the speed at which lift and drag were measured; not a flight speed

rect.title: 3.87 to 5.15 m/s. estimated. Source: makiguchi-2013 (Table 1; Table 3; Discussion), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:16:19Z. Method: captive aquarium with 3-axis accelerometer; leap speed estimated from tail-beat frequency 21.2 Hz by Wardle's formula. mean fork length 325.0 +- 11.4 mm and mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 fish; pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg; authors say the aquarium limited performance so speeds are below field values

10 to 20 m/s. secondary. Source: park-choi-2010 (Introduction citing Hertel 1966; Fish 1990; Davenport 1994), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:18:51Z. Method: field observation; quoted second-hand. maximum flight speed in the region of 10 to 20 m/s; the three primary sources were not fetched

circle.title: 10 m/s. secondary. Source: makiguchi-2013 (Introduction citing Edgerton and Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:16:19Z. Method: stroboscopic film; quoted second-hand. leap from the surface at about 10 m/s; glide up to 50 m at 15 to 20 m/s airspeed

rect.title: 15 to 20 m/s. secondary. Source: makiguchi-2013 (Introduction citing Edgerton and Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:16:19Z. Method: stroboscopic film; quoted second-hand. leap from the surface at about 10 m/s; glide up to 50 m at 15 to 20 m/s airspeed

circle.title: 20 m/s. theory-secondary. Source: deng-2019 (Introduction citing Hertel 1966), retrieved 2026-10-31T18:17:47Z. Method: theoretical trajectory (Hertel 1966); quoted second-hand. 48 m and about 10 m height are Hertel's calculated trajectory for 20 m/s airspeed into a 10 m/s headwind; not an observation
